6c32b24f39ccd8ad: KUALA LUMPUR: The Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) will appeal against blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris's acquittal in a sedition case over alleged remarks that the government was pro-Israel.

In a statement, the A-GC said it had decided to file a notice of appeal after reviewing the Sessions Court's decision to acquit and discharge Wan Azri, 43, better known as Papagomo, at the close of his defence case.
The AGC said the Sessions Court had initially acquitted Wan Azri on Sept 3, 2025, at the close of the prosecution's case.
However, the prosecution appealed against the decision, and the High Court allowed the appeal on July 31, ruling that a prima facie case had been established.
The High Court then ordered Wan Azri to enter his defence before Sessions Court judge Siti Aminah Ghazali, who was sitting in Klang.
Wan Azri testified under oath as the sole defence witness.
The A-GC said Wan Azri admitted to making the statement for which he was charged but presented what it described as a bare denial in his defence.
"After reviewing the Sessions Court judge's decision to acquit and discharge him at the end of his defence case today, the A-GC has decided to file a notice of appeal in the near future," it said.
Wan Azri was charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act.
He had pleaded not guilty to allegedly making seditious remarks in a Facebook post on Nov 8, 2023, claiming that the government was pro-Israel.
f54e0b427f18388b: WASHINGTON: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Monday that he would give every child in the United States a share in his SpaceX rocket company.
"Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America," Musk, the richest man in the world, said on X.
"This will be the first of many," he said, without providing details about how the scheme would work.
There are around 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to 2024 data from the US Census Bureau.
Musk owns 38 per cent of SpaceX, according to Forbes.
His announcement comes after President Donald Trump promised last month to give every American adult US$5,000 if his Republican party retains control of Congress in November's midterm elections.
SpaceX set the record for the largest initial public offering in history, raising US$85.7 billion in June.
The company's Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the rocket central to Musk's Mars ambitions.
832ea60088ac6b52: KUCHING, Oct 19 — The proposed New Kuching International Airport (NKIA) at Tanjung Embang could contribute approximately RM1.8 billion annually to Sarawak’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2050 under a high-growth scenario.
Sarawak Minister for Transport Datuk Seri Lee Kim Shin said the projection was among the findings of a feasibility study conducted by Netherlands Airport Consultants (NACO).

“The study also projected that NKIA could support approximately 37,919 full-time equivalent jobs across the wider economy. During construction, Phase One could support around 9,393 jobs annually over the projected six-year construction period.

“NKIA has the potential to create wider economic opportunities in tourism, aviation services and supporting industries, including air cargo, aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO), aircraft parts manufacturing, as well as aerotropolis development,” he said.
Lee said this when winding up the debate for his ministry at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting here, today.
He said the completed study has concluded that Tanjung Embang is technically and operationally feasible for the proposed airport development.

“The study also projects that increased passenger traffic could generate RM3.99 billion in tourism receipts by 2050. These benefits could attract new investments, strengthen local businesses, create employment opportunities and stimulate economic growth across Sarawak,” he added. — Bernama
e208d2ff5d2d6dc9: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has ordered the government to return about 176 Bitcoins (BTC) to nine victims of the Bitkingdom cryptocurrency investment scam.
The cryptocurrency forms part of the 497.82 BTC, valued at US$17.64 million as of Nov 1, 2023, seized from two digital wallets belonging to Mohammad Fadino Khairuman and Arsyan Ismail.

Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin made the order after finding that the nine people who had invested in the scheme between 2015 and 2016 had legitimate ownership rights over the seized cryptocurrency.

In his grounds of judgment dated Oct 12, he said the claimants had proven that they were deceived into depositing their Bitcoins into Bitkingdom, which had promised daily returns of about one per cent.
He said the cryptocurrency was transferred from the Bitkingdom wallet through several intermediary wallets before ending up in digital wallets belonging to Fadino and Arsyan.
Arief said the transfers, described as a "layering process", did not extinguish the victims' ownership rights over the cryptocurrency.
"The claimants did not lend their Bitcoins to the respondents, and they are not asserting a debt.
"They are saying that the Bitcoins were obtained from them by cheating, and that the Bitcoins, or what now stands in its place, is still theirs," he said.
Arief said property obtained through fraud did not become the legitimate property of the fraudster simply because it had been transferred to another account.
"Where property is obtained by fraud, the law does not treat the fraudster as acquiring a clean title to it as against the person defrauded."

Arief rejected the prosecution's argument that the claimants could not establish legitimate legal interests in the seized cryptocurrency as the Bitcoins had been transferred through several wallets and mixed with other digital assets.
The judge said accepting such an argument would effectively allow fraudsters to deprive their victims of their property by laundering the proceeds of their crimes.
The judge said there was also insufficient evidence to establish that the claimants had participated in, colluded in or were involved in the cheating or money laundering activities.

He ruled that all nine claimants had established legitimate legal interests in the seized cryptocurrency under Section 61(4) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).

However, Arief said the claimants were not entitled to recover the full amount of Bitcoins they had deposited as the total losses suffered by Bitkingdom investors exceeded the cryptocurrency seized by the authorities.
The court was told that 207 police reports had been lodged by investors involving losses totalling approximately 1,023 BTC.
The nine claimants had collectively deposited 362.04 BTC into the scheme.
Based on the amount seized, the judge ruled that they were entitled to recover a proportionate share amounting to approximately 176.18 BTC.
The remaining seized cryptocurrency, estimated at 321.64 BTC, is to be forfeited to the government under Section 56(2) of AMLA.

On Dec 23 last year, the High Court ruled that the seized cryptocurrency constituted proceeds of unlawful activities involving cheating under Section 420 of the Penal Code through the Bitkingdom investment platform.

b2b2e60f0298a3ee: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan perlu mempertimbangkan sumbangan AirAsia kepada sektor pelancongan dan ekonomi negara sebelum memutuskan sama ada mahu memberikan bantuan kepada syarikat penerbangan tambang murah itu, kata seorang Ahli Parlimen.

Ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027, Larry Sng (PBM-Julau) berkata syarikat itu memainkan peranan penting dalam menghubungkan rakyat, menyokong pelancongan dan menyediakan pilihan penerbangan yang mampu milik.

"Kerajaan patut mempertimbangkan kepentingan kesambungan udara sektor pelancongan dan sumbangannya kepada ekonomi negara sebelum membuat sebarang keputusan mengenai bantuan tersebut,” katanya di Dewan Rakyat.
Sng berkata operasi syarikat penerbangan itu penting bagi memastikan perjalanan udara kekal mampu diakses oleh orang ramai.
"Jika AirAsia tutup, saya fikir 'not everyone can fly'. Saya berpandangan bahawa memastikan AirAsia terus beroperasi adalah penting demi kepentingan ekonomi negara," katanya.

Minggu lalu, Reuters melaporkan bahawa pengasas bersama AirAsia, Tony Fernandes, bertemu pegawai Kementerian Kewangan dan Kementerian Pengangkutan untuk membincangkan kos berkaitan penerbangan, di tengah-tengah kebimbangan mengenai kedudukan kewangan syarikat itu.

Laporan itu, yang memetik tiga individu yang mengetahui perkara tersebut, menyatakan bahawa perbincangan turut tertumpu pada kemungkinan kerajaan menyokong usaha AirAsia mengumpul dana, tertakluk pada syarat dicadangkan dan masih dalam perbincangan.

Bagaimanapun, Fernandes berkata pertemuan itu tertumpu pada kos berkaitan penerbangan, termasuk caj lapangan terbang dan bahan api, dan tiada perbincangan mengenai bantuan kewangan. Fernandes juga menafikan bahawa beliau meminta bantuan daripada kerajaan.
Fernandes berkata beliau kekal yakin bahawa AirAsia mampu mengharungi tempoh sukar itu tanpa bantuan kerajaan, tetapi menambah bahawa syarikat itu tidak akan menolak bantuan sekiranya ditawarkan.

Syarikat itu terjejas akibat kenaikan kos bahan api jet dan melaporkan kerugian bersih sebanyak RM831 juta bagi suku kedua yang berakhir pada 30 Jun, sebahagiannya disebabkan oleh perbelanjaan bahan api yang lebih tinggi dan kerugian pertukaran wang asing.

Reuters turut melaporkan bahawa AirAsia sedang berusaha mengumpul sehingga USD1 bilion daripada pasaran hutang antarabangsa dan mendapatkan kemudahan kredit tempatan sebanyak RM700 juta, terutamanya untuk membiayai semula hutang sedia ada.
25326e77e0356285: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) will file a notice of appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision to acquit and discharge blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, also known as Papagomo, of a sedition charge.

In a statement today, the AGC said the decision was made after examining the ruling of the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court sitting in the Klang Sessions Court today, which acquitted and discharged Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, at the close of the defence case for a charge under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948 (Act 15).

“After examining the decision of the Sessions Court Judge, this department has decided to file a notice of appeal against the acquittal and discharge in the near future,” the AGC said in a statement today.

According to the AGC, the prosecution had previously appealed against a decision by the same court on September 3, 2025, which had acquitted and discharged the accused at the close of the prosecution’s case.

The AGC stated that the appeal against that decision was filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on September 4, 2025, before the court allowed the public prosecutor’s appeal on July 31 last year and ordered the accused to enter his defence after finding that the prosecution had successfully proven a prima facie case.

“The accused presented his defence by giving sworn testimony in the same Sessions Court. The accused, who was the sole defence witness, admitted to issuing seditious statements as charged and merely presented a defence in the form of a denial,” the AGC said in the statement.
Earlier, Judge Siti Aminah Ghazali acquitted and discharged Wan Muhammad Azri after finding that the defence had successfully raised reasonable doubt at the close of the defence case.
On January 8, 2024, the man pleaded not guilty to a charge of uttering seditious remarks linking the government to being pro-Israel and pro-West via Facebook.

He was allegedly accused of making the statement on the Facebook page of Halid Hamidi (Halid Mat Kool), which was later viewed by an individual at a condominium unit in Jalan Tong Shin, Bukit Bintang here at 1pm on November 8, 2023.
The charge was framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, which carries a maximum penalty of three years in imprisonment or a fine of RM5,000, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama
23b1197396d92bdc: PETALING JAYA: The Land Public Transport Agency (Apad) has drawn criticism after deciding to limit express bus ticket sales to Apad-licensed bus terminals from Nov 1.
Pan Malaysian Bus Operators Association president Ashfar Ali said he received a letter from Apad dated Oct 16 about the new rule and the association was "caught flatfooted".
“We were not consulted or asked about anything. We do not know why this was done,” he told FMT, adding that he is pushing for a meeting with Apad over the matter.
Ashfar argued that this new rule was unfair to customers, as online agents could offer better prices through deals with bus operators, benefiting users.
“Passengers can jump from one online agent to another to compare pricing. They might lose that flexibility now.”
He also said bus operators have spent money developing their own websites and online ticketing systems, which would go to waste once the new rule takes effect.

In the circular, Apad said express bus terminals have been given absolute rights over ticket sales for passengers using their services, which meant trip management and sales transactions would fall under the responsibility of terminals.
The agency also said a new commercial charge for digital platform services will be imposed on bus operators, not passengers, with the rate to be reviewed periodically.
According to the New Straits Times, Apad said tickets could still be purchased through online travel agencies or bus operators’ websites if the operators owned the terminals outright.
However, Ashfar said most terminals are owned by private companies or the government.

d0e83a7f0c206e01: SEMPORNA, Oct 19 — The issue of foreigners abusing social visit passes to engage in illegal economic activities in Semporna has been raised and discussed in the Federal Cabinet, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.

He said the federal government takes the situation seriously and is actively carrying out enforcement action through integrated operations, particularly on popular tourist islands in the waters off the district.
“Action is being taken on this issue, with operations conducted particularly against business activities on the islands.

“The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) has also discussed this issue and will take appropriate action,” he told reporters after an official working visit today to assess border control preparedness at Pulau Ligitan, Pulau Sipadan and Pulau Mabul.

He was commenting on a special report series by the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) published in August, which highlighted how foreign investors were illegally gaining control of the district’s tourism economic chain, posing a serious threat to the security and livelihoods of the local population.

According to the reports, the Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCom) also exposed how foreigners used illegal partnerships or local proxies in “Ali Baba” arrangements to control services, resorts, and tourism facilities, creating opportunities for various criminal activities, including operating scam centres.

Commenting on the same reports, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he had directed ESSCom to conduct joint enforcement operations with all relevant parties in the area, including local authorities. — Bernama
3481759666f209cb: KUALA LUMPUR: KFC Malaysia has contributed 20,000 face masks to support vulnerable and underserved communities across the Klang Valley amid recent air quality concerns.
The contribution was made in collaboration with Kechara Soup Kitchen (KSK) and The Lost Food Project (TLFP), both partners of the company's KFC Harvest Programme.
QSR Brands (M) Holdings Bhd head of governance Sahada Salihin said the contribution reflected the company's commitment to supporting communities beyond its food business.

"We believe that our responsibility extends beyond serving great meals. We are committed to being a positive force in the communities we serve and supporting those who face daily challenges," she said in a statement.
She added that working with the non-governmental organisations (NGOs) would help ensure assistance reached those who needed it most.
The ceremony was held at Menara QSR, where representatives from both NGO partners received the face masks on behalf of the communities they serve.
The contribution marks the beginning of a two-phase outreach effort aimed at providing additional care and protection to individuals facing hardship.
The first phase involves distributing the face masks through the partners' outreach networks, including to homeless people and underserved families.

KFC Malaysia representatives also joined volunteers from both organisations in distributing face masks and KFC meal packs to the homeless community at Pusat Khidmat Gelandangan Medan Tuanku, Kuala Lumpur on Oct 17.
KSK and TLFP collectively reach nearly 8,000 beneficiaries across the Klang Valley, including residents of charity homes and People's Housing Programme communities with outreach extending nationwide.

The second phase will be incorporated into upcoming KFC Harvest Programme activities, where beneficiaries at participating charity homes and community centres will receive face masks, freshly prepared KFC meals and frozen chicken.
Sahada said the initiative complemented the company's food redistribution efforts through the Harvest Programme.
"Together with our partners, we hope to continue creating a meaningful and lasting impact for the communities we serve," she said.
Introduced in Malaysia in 2019, the KFC Harvest Programme rescues surplus food from participating restaurants and redistributes it through NGO partners to underserved communities and charity homes.
The programme now covers 170 KFC restaurants nationwide and has redistributed more than 61,000 kilograms of surplus food, benefiting thousands of individuals and families across Malaysia.

d2d7a7b571348193: PETALING JAYA: Schools in Melaka, Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, as well as those in Kuantan, Rompin and Bentong in Pahang, will open as usual tomorrow, but all outdoor activities have been suspended because of the haze.

The Melaka, Selangor and Negeri Sembilan education departments said students were encouraged to wear face masks, while parents or guardians concerned about their children’s health were allowed to keep them at home, provided they informed the school, Bernama reported.
They said school administrators must continuously monitor the air pollutant index (API) readings from the environment department, and pay special attention to high-risk students.
In separate statements, the departments also advised the public to refer to official channels or the schools for the latest information.
In Pahang, the education department said schools in Kuantan, Rompin and Bentong would open tomorrow, but all outdoor and out-of-classroom activities had been cancelled.
“Any changes will be communicated from time to time through the respective district education offices,” it said in a Facebook post.

Earlier today, the education ministry announced an extension of the deadline for entering marks for several school assessments in the Integrated Education Management System, following disruptions to school sessions and assessment activities because of the haze.

The deadline for entering marks for the end-of-academic session assessment, and examinations has been extended from Nov 21 to Nov 28, while the new deadline for entering marks for the physical, sports and co-curricular assessment is Dec 5 instead of the previous Nov 30.
bcc76f2715a6aa15: CEUTA: When heavily pregnant Fatna and her disabled son arrived in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta during a chaotic mass border crossing on July 30, she hoped to be high on authorities' list for help.
Nearly three months later, with her newborn baby girl suffering from kidney problems, Fatna, 21, and her family urgently need to reach mainland Spain for specialist hospital treatment.

However, travelling while her asylum claim is under review requires a permit that Spain's socialist government – ordinarily a staunch advocate of immigration – has been reluctant to grant to any of the thousands of migrants remaining in Ceuta.
Some are still scattered on the streets or hiding in the rolling hills of the tiny 20sqkm port city on Morocco's northeast border.
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's government is under pressure from the EU and an increasingly frustrated populace to sort out the crisis and faces a snap election on Nov 29.
It is working on shortcuts for asylum applications with the intention of sending most people home, mainly to Morocco, on the basis of being economic migrants not real asylum-seekers.
That, NGOs fear, risks violating migrants' rights.
Sanchez, one of Europe's few remaining left-leaning leaders, said this week that Spain was managing the flood of cases "responsibly, with a sense of solidarity and respecting migrants' human rights".

However, more than 20 interviews by Reuters with migrants, lawyers, NGOs, and security forces revealed that many of those who remain have clear grounds for asylum or humanitarian protection: from unaccompanied minors to LGBT Moroccans fearing imprisonment if deported and families like Fatna's classified as vulnerable under EU law.
Last week, eight charities including Oxfam and Amnesty International filed a complaint with Spain's ombudsman, seen by Reuters, alleging "grave rights violations" in the tiny Ceuta enclave.
They included the forced return of migrants from conflict-hit countries and denial of interpreters and legal assistance.
Spokespeople for Spain's central government, interior ministry, territorial policy ministry and migration ministry did not respond to Reuters requests for comment on the mistreatment accusations.

"There are people who will truly be in enormous danger if they are returned to Morocco," said Wendell Soares, coordinator of the Catholic migrant reception centre San Antonio, which has taken in Fatna's family and dozens more vulnerable people, far beyond its usual capacity of seven.
"When the word ‘immigrant’ is used, it creates a collective image, as if they were all the same. Every person has their own story," Soares said.
Deported without explanation
Spanish right-wing and far-right parties were already angry with Sanchez's government for providing legal status to nearly 1 million irregular migrants earlier this year.
They have cast July's crossing as a deliberate invasion by Morocco – an accusation Morocco denies – and demanded that all migrants be returned.
However, despite plans for a new EU-wide procedure enabling accelerated deportations in future emergency scenarios, current rules require that migrants be assessed case-by-case.

While most are from Morocco, the government estimated in August that more than 1,000 of the migrants remaining were from sub-Saharan countries whose nationals are granted asylum in over 90% of cases in Spain, according to government statistics.
The EU's new pact requires that cases be processed in border zones to permit faster deportations.

However, it does not require applicants to stay where they arrived, allowing for transfers to other border zones in Spain that would alleviate pressure on the 84,000-person enclave of Ceuta, Europe's only land border with Africa.
If vulnerable migrants' cases are to be properly assessed, such transfers are the "only option", said Juan Miguel Morales, director-general of NGO Sur Acoge.

While 262 minors have been transferred to the Spanish mainland since the July crossing, the government's strategy for the remaining adults has been to convince as many as possible to return of their own volition.
The government said this week that 12,000 had chosen to cross back since mid-August.

"There are no covert deportations under any circumstances," Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said, describing the returns as voluntary and adding that up to 1,200 asylum applications had been received and 700 of them resolved.
However, at least nine NGOs have in public communication or interviews with Reuters claimed that migrants they support were coerced to return.
Asociación Elin said migrants from Sudan and Chad were summoned by police on Sept 24 and 25 and deported without warning, according to the complaint to the ombudsman.

In text messages reviewed by Reuters, Moroccan migrant Azhaar Chaouni told volunteers at German NGO Mission Lifeline that he and other migrants faced the same fate, after being picked up in buses by police from their makeshift camps on the beach and told they were being taken to reception centres.
"They deported us without explanation," Chaouni wrote, saying he was in Morocco.

Morocco's designation as a "safe country of origin" under EU rules does not strip its citizens of the right to apply for asylum, said Andrea de Petris, immigration expert at Brussels-based think tank CEPN.
"Each individual must be guaranteed a specific assessment of their personal circumstances," added De Petris who estimates the procedure would inevitably be "lengthy and costly".
Stories of others disappearing have instilled fear in Rayane, a 19-year-old gay Moroccan awaiting news on his asylum application in the San Antonio reception centre.
Rejected by his family and unable to live openly in Morocco where same-sex sexual acts are prosecuted, he is desperate to get to mainland Europe.
"I can’t even imagine myself going back to Morocco. I’d kill myself before even crossing the border," he said.
Pact exposed

Frontline workers and NGOs on the ground say the situation in Ceuta has proven that the 12-week limit set in the EU’s migrant pact for processing asylum applications is unrealistic, with seven stating they expect the process to drag on for months.
A lack of resources from staff to functioning computers meant that only around 100 migrants' cases were being registered daily by Oct 14, according to police union representative Raul Piera.

The union estimates roughly 7,000-8,000 more migrants are still scattered across the city, sleeping rough or squeezed into facilities provided by charities and civil society groups filling the gap left by Ceuta's overwhelmed social services.
"Looking at the remaining workload, this will last well into next summer," said Piera.

Spain's government has declined to comment on estimates of unregistered migrants, with territorial policy minister Angel Victor Torres telling reporters on Oct 14 that it was impossible to know how many were hiding.

Doctors in Ceuta's only hospital are treating migrants for scabies, tuberculosis and gastrointestinal infections caused by long periods outdoors, said Enrique Robiralta, head of the doctors' union. At least seven women have given birth.

Fatna and her husband Mohamed are desperate to stay in Spain, fearing for the new baby and convinced their 3-year-old disabled son will die in Morocco. "We are doing everything for our son," said Mohamed.
df1c27c6efd8d4bb: KUALA LUMPUR: UDA Holdings Bhd has allocated RM5 million to develop public parks and recreational facilities in Penang, including a 1.01-hectare public park in Tanjung Tokong.
The park, Laman Tanjong, will be located next to the Eight & Eight Condominium development and is intended to provide recreational space for residents and the surrounding community.

Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said the initiative aimed to ensure new property developments also benefited nearby communities by improving access to public spaces and supporting residents' well-being.
He added that cooperation between the federal and state governments, together with implementing agencies such as UDA, was important in delivering urban developments that meet community needs.
Sim also said new housing developments could create economic opportunities for local entrepreneurs as growing populations generated demand for goods and services.

UDA chief executive officer Ahmad Fuaad Kenali said the company had contributed to Penang's urban development since 1971, particularly in Tanjung Tokong, through residential projects, commercial developments and supporting infrastructure.

"Our developments have been driven by the objective of improving the living standards of previous residents through the resettlement project into a modern, inclusive and sustainable community," he said.

Among its projects in the area is Warisan Tanjung, which comprises 3,836 residential units across 17.58 hectares, including 1,200 replacement homes for original Tanjung Tokong residents under a resettlement initiative.
UDA also developed Desiran Tanjung, a 21.88-hectares residential and commercial development that includes about 120 shop-office units at Vantage Desiran Tanjung along Jalan Tanjung Tokong.
The area's latest development, Eight & Eight Condominium, comprises 600 residential units across two towers and is scheduled for completion in 2029.
The condominium offers three-bedroom units ranging from 885 to 1,139 square feet, with prices starting at RM691,628.

Facilities include a swimming pool, gymnasium, prayer hall, multipurpose hall, co-working space and electric vehicle charging bays. The development also incorporates features such as rainwater harvesting, herb gardens and green landscaping.

It is located near healthcare facilities including Penang Adventist Hospital, Gleneagles Hospital Penang and Penang General Hospital, as well as schools, shopping centres and recreational attractions.

0b6453ed897a8abf: PETALING JAYA: Rapid KL will deploy 85 buses for a special shuttle service to Sepang International Circuit (SIC) from Oct 30 to Nov 1, in conjunction with the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix.
Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd CEO Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said tickets would go on sale from Oct 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni bus hub.
“Every year, motorsports fans from various locations gather in Sepang to experience the excitement of this world-class race firsthand.
“Rapid KL hopes this service will make their journeys to the circuit easier and more comfortable,” he was quoted as saying by Bernama today.
Syahrul said the shuttle service would operate from the Pasar Seni bus hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 bus hub.
A one-way ticket from Pasar Seni or the KLCC bus stop will cost RM20, while a return ticket will be priced at RM35. The one-way fare from KLIA Terminal 2 is RM12.
Buses travelling to SIC from all three locations will operate from 7am to 1pm at 30-minute intervals, while return services from the circuit will run from 4pm to 7pm.
In collaboration with SIC, Rapid KL will also provide a free shuttle service around the circuit throughout the event to facilitate visitor movement.

a1404fd07eb4ad2b: SEOUL, Oct 19 — The powerful sister of North Korea’s leader said today that “a grave situation is prevailing” along the Southern border, according to state media, and Pyongyang was considering deploying “more tactical strike means” to the area.

The announcement comes amid heightened tensions between the two Koreas, with the nuclear-armed North stepping up weapons tests in recent days, including of a “new-type” precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence to detect and track targets.
“Now the situation of the southern border is very unstable,” Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said in a statement.

“A grave situation is prevailing along the southern border due to the reckless behavior of the ROK military gangsters,” she said in the English-language statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency.
Citing South Korea’s firing of warning shots, broadcasts from propaganda loudspeakers and what she called a “mine explosion farce”, Kim said the incidents had “gone beyond the red line”.

North Korea has rejected claims it was behind an explosion that injured three soldiers last month inside the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ), the heavily mined buffer area that has divided the two Koreas since their 1953 armistice.
A joint Seoul-United Nations Command investigation concluded the blast was caused by North Korean mines laid on the South Korean side of the border.

“Our military leadership is examining the issues of deploying more tactical strike means along the southern border as a preemptive and suppressive measure to deal with contingency,” said Kim, but did not specify the details of the tactical strike.
Kim also added that the North is reviewing “resuming the loudspeaker broadcasting against the ROK and considering other necessary and appropriate measures”.
She warned that if the actions were to continue, “Seoul will surely regret and face uncontrollably terrible danger”.
In 2024, North Korea sent thousands of trash-carrying balloons southwards, saying they were retaliation for anti-North propaganda balloons floated by South Korean activists.

Later, the South turned on border loudspeaker broadcasts for the first time in six years — including K-pop tunes and international news — and the North started transmitting strange sounds along the frontier, unsettling South Korean residents.
Loudspeaker broadcasts, a tactic that dates back to the Korean War, have previously prompted Pyongyang to threaten artillery strikes on Seoul’s speaker units.
South Korea’s President Lee Jae Myung has vowed to reach out to the nuclear-armed North and pursue dialogue without preconditions — a reversal from his hawkish predecessor.
Last year the South’s defence ministry removed loudspeakers from its side of the border as “a practical measure aimed at helping ease tensions with the North”. — AFP

3ba30b3049864bee: MANILA: The Philippine foreign ministry summoned Beijing's ambassador to Manila on Monday after he said China would "easily win" a conflict between the countries, with local senators calling for his expulsion.

8a8c003fa0856d2a: KUCHING, Oct 19 — Sarawak aims for an electricity generation capacity of 15,000 megawatts (MW) by 2035, with at least 60 per cent coming from renewable energy sources.

148f1abb9453cee0: SINGAPORE, Oct 19 — Senior Minister K Shanmugam has taken issue with an Indonesian official’s remarks that Singapore’s oxygen “comes from [their] forests”, saying it was “not right” to make such comments while the region was suffering from haze caused by companies breaching regulations in Indonesia.

Speaking at a doorstop today, the coordinating minister for national security and minister for home affairs said: “Frankly, it is not right to say this when this entire region is suffering as a result of the bad behaviour of companies breaching regulations in Indonesia. And the people suffering the most are Indonesians themselves.”
His remarks appeared to reject any suggestion that Singapore should have to tolerate the haze simply because Indonesia’s forests also contribute to the region’s air quality.
Shanmugam said Singaporeans were deeply frustrated by the worsening haze situation, which was affecting public health and was entirely preventable.

He reiterated Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s statement last Thursday, where PM Wong shared that Singapore would — if necessary — take legal action under Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act against companies contributing to haze.
“The haze is affecting our health seriously… It is really unacceptable,” Shanmugam said.
He added that he did not believe the Indonesian official’s view was shared by many others in the Indonesian government or the broader public.
“We shouldn’t have to put up with this - the smog as a result of the burning,” he added. “It is entirely preventable.”
“We must also be clear about where responsibility for this lies,” Shanmugam said, adding that the haze was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits.

Responding to suggestions that legal action against companies linked to the haze could have diplomatic implications, Shanmugam said Singapore could not afford to hold back when its people were suffering.
“What do these experts think we are supposed to do? Shiver in our shoes before we take any action to protect our own people? That’s not the Singapore approach.
“If we think like that, there will be no Singapore, and we do not think there should be any bilateral issues.”
He added that the Indonesian public was also suffering from the haze, and that it was in Indonesia’s interests as much as Singapore’s to deal with the companies responsible for the fires.
“The Indonesian public is suffering as well, and it is in Indonesia’s interests as much as ours to deal with the companies that are causing these problems.”

Shanmugam said Singapore’s actions against companies believed to be responsible for the fires were aligned with the broad policies announced by the Indonesian administration under President Prabowo Subianto.
He also welcomed efforts by Indonesian President Prabowo and his administration to tackle the haze, highlighting several measures that have already been taken.

These include replacing the head of the agency overseeing firefighting and disaster relief, directing that slash-and-burn practices on peatland be prohibited, and prioritising fire prevention as a long-term solution.
“Some of these steps are quite unprecedented. They show what President Prabowo and his administration’s approach and thinking are,” SM Shanmugam said.
“We also welcome President Prabowo’s approval of foreign assistance to combat the fires. We, Singapore, have offered our assistance, and we will do our part to support.

“In fact, we hope to get full cooperation from Indonesia in going after the companies, and likewise, we have also offered our full cooperation in assisting to put out the fires, insofar as our assistance is required.” — AsiaOne
29c4682f7c90ade3: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Malaysia has retained the World Health Organisation (WHO) validation for the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis following an assessment of the country’s achievements from 2021 to 2024.

In a statement, the Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement reaffirmed the recognition first obtained in 2018, when Malaysia became the first country in the WHO Western Pacific Region to receive the validation.
The ministry said the recognition reflected Malaysia’s continued commitment to strengthening maternal and child health and ensuring access to quality screening, treatment and healthcare services.

It added that the achievement demonstrated the effectiveness of the Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission (PMTCT) of HIV and Syphilis programme, which has been integrated into the country’s maternal and child health services since 1997.
The certificate and recognition were received by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad at the 77th WHO Regional Committee for the Western Pacific meeting in Manila today.

According to the MOH, screening coverage for HIV and syphilis among pregnant women remained above 95 per cent throughout the assessment period, while antiretroviral treatment coverage among pregnant women living with HIV reached approximately 99 per cent.
In 2024, the mother-to-child HIV transmission rate stood at 1.52 per cent, meeting the WHO target of below two per cent.

The ministry also reported that the rate of congenital syphilis, an infection transmitted from mother to child during pregnancy, stood at 10 cases per 100,000 live births, well below the WHO elimination threshold of 50 cases per 100,000 live births.

The MOH attributed the achievement to the sustained commitment of healthcare personnel at all levels and collaboration among government agencies, private healthcare providers, the Malaysian AIDS Council, civil society organisations and the community.
The ministry also expressed appreciation to all parties involved, as well as the WHO, for its technical support and cooperation.
It said efforts would continue to strengthen early detection, treatment and follow-up care for mothers and infants to sustain the achievement.

The MOH also advised pregnant women to seek antenatal care as early as possible and complete the recommended screening and treatment procedures to protect their health and that of their babies. — Bernama

f0c9552ff336a3ab: SINGAPORE, Oct 19 — Companies linked to ongoing wildfires in Indonesia that have blanketed several South-east Asian countries in hazardous haze have been urged to cooperate with the Singapore Government. Those that refuse could face pressure on their financing, investor standing and bottom line, Senior Minister K Shanmugam warned.
“We will use every legal and regulatory lever at our disposal to exert pressure where it matters,” Shanmugam said today, as he spoke to the media during a visit to Woodlands Checkpoint.

Shanmugam, who is also coordinating minister for national security and minister for home affairs, noted that the Singapore Exchange (SGX) has asked questions of seven agri-related companies listed in Singapore.
The seven companies are: Golden-Agri Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri, and TSH Resources.
When asked what could happen if these companies refused to cooperate, Shanmugam cautioned that they should not underestimate the Singapore Government’s determination to act.

“If companies refuse to cooperate, regardless of whether they have a presence in Singapore, or do not have a presence in Singapore, we will use every legal and regulatory lever at our disposal to exert pressure where it matters,” the senior minister said.
He added that this includes their bottom-line, access to financing and standing with investors.
If necessary, the Government could also amend existing legislation or introduce new laws on an urgent basis to ensure greater cooperation, Shanmugam said.
Companies cannot ‘greenwash’ behaviour
The senior minister also emphasised that companies cannot simply claim to be environmentally responsible, while refusing to subject themselves to scrutiny.
“Their claims must be backed by evidence, not just words. They cannot greenwash their behaviour,” he said.
Shanmugam also warned such companies that they cannot simply wait for the haze to clear, and return to what he described as “business as usual”.
“We will pursue this matter for as long as it takes,” he said.

Meanwhile, the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, along with other agencies, have taken several steps to deal with the ground situation, including distribution of N95 haze masks to vulnerable Singaporeans.
At the same time, the authorities are examining what further action can be taken against companies that may be linked to the fires.
The Homefront Crisis Ministerial Committee, chaired by Shanmugam, is also looking into the issue.
“Dealing with these companies is one of those issues,” Shanmugam said.
Shanmugam said the haze was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits, adding that those responsible must be held accountable.

While speaking to the media, the senior minister also referred to comments made by the Indonesian Head of Government Communications Agency Syahganda Nainggolan, who told media there on October 10 that Indonesia also sends oxygen to Malaysia and Singapore.
Shanmugam said it was “not right” to make such remarks when the region was suffering from haze caused by companies breaching regulations in Indonesia.

“Frankly, it is not right to say this when this entire region is suffering as a result of the bad behaviour of companies breaching regulations in Indonesia,” Shanmugam said, pointing out that Indonesians are suffering the most. — AsiaOne
7fae483315f06e4c: Today's entry in the catalog of bork comes from Coventry's Herbert Art Gallery & Museum, where an information terminal is showing more about the hardware behind the scenes than the objects on display. Register reader Jeffrey Borinsky spotted the panel, which should have demonstrated a Jacquard loom in action but was instead displaying a warning about its host PC's failing battery. The Jacquard loom was a clever device dating back to the dawn of the 19th century. It used punched cards to control a loom's weaving patterns. The result was complicated and repeatable textile designs that reduced the need for skilled humans. Register readers of a certain age are doubtless nodding sagely at the mention of punched cards, which would go on to become foundational in the world of computing. Borinsky reported that several screens at the museum were in distress. Ribbon weaving was Coventry's main industry from the early 1700s until the 1860s, so a demonstration of Jacquard weaving fits right in, even if the bleating about the BIOS battery was probably not what Joseph Jacquard had in mind. The device running behind the scenes is a Dell OptiPlex 755, likely from around 2007. Not quite centuries old like a Jacquard loom, but certainly getting on a bit in the IT world. The first iPhone arrived in 2007, and a PC of a similar vintage likely shipped with Windows XP or Windows Vista. The CMOS battery is on the way out. Dell specifies a CR2032 coin cell, so replacement should be straightforward after disconnecting the power and taking anti-static precautions. Rather less traumatic than the head-in-hands moment when a retro enthusiast discovers a leaking battery has eaten through delicate circuit traces. A fresh battery and restored BIOS settings should be enough to get the loom demonstration weaving again. Given how important punched cards became in the history of computing, we'd recommend visiting anywhere that shows how a Jacquard loom operated. At least it didn't need a battery-backed BIOS to do its thing. ®

e03009f01173e2e3: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — The government plans to draft the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill for submission to the Cabinet next year to regulate the growth of the data centre industry in line with the country’s energy and water supply capacity.

Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the measure aims to ensure that investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy, in addition to addressing utility constraints and avoiding imbalances in environmental impact.

He said the proposal to draft the bill is part of the strategic regulatory plan agreed upon by the National Economic Action Council (NEAC) at a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today.
He said the agreement was reached following the presentation of the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development by the Ministry of Digital.

“This step is taken to address utility constraints, avoid environmental impact imbalances, and ensure that data centre investments provide real economic spillovers to the local digital ecosystem,” he said in a statement.
Akmal Nasrullah said NEAC also agreed that the four lead ministries, along with the implementing agencies, would adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Ministry of Economy.

“NEAC agreed that the lead ministries, namely the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, and the Ministry of Human Resources, along with the implementing agencies, should adopt the CEF with an integrated governance, monitoring, and coordination structure,” he said.

He noted that the framework aims to lead the country’s transition from a linear economic model based on the “use-and-dispose” concept to a circular economy that optimises the lifespan of materials, reduces waste and preserves the value of resources.

“This integrated policy was formulated to address the issue of fragmented implementation across ministries in the past, to avoid economic losses due to the loss of valuable resources, and to support the Net Zero aspiration by 2050,” he said.

In other developments, Akmal Nasrullah said the meeting also reviewed the National Economic Resilience Framework presented by the Economic Affairs Division, Prime Minister’s Office, as a comprehensive long-term measure to address external economic shocks.

“The meeting agreed that this proposal should be presented to the Cabinet and further discussed at a meeting of ministry secretaries-general and heads of service chaired by the Chief Secretary to the Government,” he said.

He highlighted that NEAC today examined three strategic policy priorities to drive sustainable growth and strengthen the resilience of the country’s economy in the face of structural challenges and global economic uncertainties.

He said the agreed policies must be implemented in an integrated manner, particularly to enhance the efficiency of resource use, ensure that data centre investments add value to the domestic economy, and strengthen the country’s preparedness to face external economic shocks.
Akmal Nasrullah said the Ministry of Economy, as the NEAC secretariat, will coordinate and monitor follow-up actions with the relevant ministries and implementing agencies.
“The government’s priority is not just growth and investment, but a more productive, sustainable, and resilient economy with real benefits for the people and businesses,” he added. — Bernama
16b4095f9e191ec4: PETALING JAYA: Ahli Parlimen Seputeh Teresa Kok menang saman fitnahnya terhadap Dr Akmal Saleh, dengan Mahkamah Tinggi memerintahkan ketua Pemuda Umno itu membayar ganti rugi berjumlah RM250,000.

ef2410216132da49: PETALING JAYA: The government is drafting a Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill and will submit it to the Cabinet next year.
Economy minister Akmal Nasir said this will help regulate the growth of the data centre industry, in line with the country's energy and water supply capacity.
Bernama reported him as saying that the bill aimed to ensure investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy, address utility constraints and avoid imbalances in environmental impact.
He said the proposal to draft the bill was part of a strategic regulatory plan agreed upon by the National Economic Action Council (MTEN) at a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim today.
He said the agreement was reached following the presentation of the national strategic direction towards sustainable data centre development by the digital ministry.

Akmal said MTEN also agreed that four lead ministries – the housing and local government ministry, the investment, trade and industry ministry, the science, technology and innovation ministry, and the human resources ministry – would adopt the circular economy framework presented by the economy ministry.

He said the framework aims to lead the country's transition from a linear economic model, based on the "use-and-dispose" concept, to a circular economy that optimises the lifespan of materials, reduces waste and preserves the value of resources.

“This integrated policy was formulated to address the issue of fragmented implementation across ministries in the past, to avoid economic losses caused by the wastage of valuable resources and to support the net zero aspiration by 2050,” he said.

Akmal said the meeting also reviewed the national economic resilience framework presented by the Prime Minister’s Office’s economic affairs division as a comprehensive long-term measure to address external economic shocks.

"The meeting agreed that the framework should be presented to the Cabinet and further discussed at a meeting of the ministries’ secretaries-general and heads of service, chaired by the chief secretary to the government," he said.
Akmal said the economy ministry, as the MTEN secretariat, will coordinate and monitor follow-up actions with the relevant ministries and implementing agencies.

18d483a912de26f8: KUWAIT CITY: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs.

Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah.

He will also visit the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Qatar by Wednesday on a trip aimed at strengthening "economic and defence partnerships" in the Gulf, which has been thrown into turmoil by the US-Iran war since February.

Macron acknowledged security and intelligence failures but refused his interior minister's resignation after more than 2,500 people were arrested in some of France's worst violence in years, with town halls and shops looted and set on fire.
Before flying to Kuwait, he said the visit was needed to "secure our supplies", pointing out that the demonstrators had expressed "concern" about fuel prices.
Macron's tour "may give an impression of normality... but may also appear out of touch and suggest a kind of power vacuum", said constitutional expert Benjamin Morel.
During his trip, "the goal is to secure a certain number of commitments" on diesel and oil volumes, the French presidency said.
Macron is accompanied by senior executives from France's two biggest energy groups, TotalEnergies and Engie.
The G7 countries, chaired this year by France, agreed in early October to draw up to 100 million barrels of oil from their strategic reserves to ease pressure.
Crude oil prices have ballooned during the eight-month war, as Iran blockades the Strait of Hormuz -- the main exit route for the Gulf's energy exports.
Yemen's Houthis have compounded the pressure by firing on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea, striking the kingdom's oil sites and carrying out deadly attacks on Riyadh's international airport.
Francis Perrin, an energy expert at the French Institute for International and Strategic Relations, said he did not expect Macron's visit to have an impact on fuel prices.
"The Arab countries of the Gulf are very eager to supply the world, and the French market, but it is difficult for them to make firm commitments until the region has been stabilised," he said.

Macron will hold talks with Gulf leaders including the UAE's president and Qatar's emir on ways to "secure" maritime shipments and find "alternative and bypass routes" for energy exports, the presidency said.
France and Britain have assembled an international mission to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, mainly through demining operations, once the United States and Iran reach agreement on the waterway.
However, the two sides remain at an impasse, eight months since the start of hostilities.
The French president will also hold talks on defence cooperation, after the Gulf countries were targeted by thousands of Iranian missiles and drones.
France deployed its aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle in the spring, along with Rafale fighter jets, a frigate and air defence assets.
Macron also sent French soldiers to protect Yanbu, an oil terminal on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast that has become a vital conduit for exports.

77d9174847ef06d2: NEW JERSEY: Sean 'Diddy' Combs has been transferred from a federal prison in New Jersey to a facility in Pennsylvania following reports of an alleged inmate altercation and claims that the music mogul enjoyed special privileges behind bars.
The 56-year-old was moved from Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix to FCI Allenwood Low, the US Bureau of Prisons confirmed.
But the agency did not disclose the reason for the transfer, citing privacy, safety and security concerns.

"Decisions about inmate placement are made by the BOP, and we are not in a position to speak to the circumstances surrounding this transfer," Combs' spokesperson, Juda Engelmayer, said in a statement.
"Sean remains focused on moving forward, and we hope that his time at the new facility will be productive and without unnecessary disruption."
The transfer followed reports that Combs had sustained a head injury during an alleged fight with another inmate and was briefly hospitalised on Oct 10.
But the Bureau of Prisons disputed a report by TMZ, telling The Associated Press that the alleged fight "is false and did not happen". Details surrounding the injury remain unclear.
Combs had also come under scrutiny following an NBC News report alleging that he enjoyed a relatively comfortable lifestyle at Fort Dix.
Citing people who had spent time in the same prison unit, the report claimed that inmates cooked meals for him, cleaned his living area, made his bed and provided massages.
He was also alleged to have accessed contraband, including alcohol and a cellphone.
Following the reports, Combs was reportedly placed in the prison's Special Housing Unit—a more restrictive section used for inmates facing disciplinary issues or security concerns.
A person familiar with the matter also told AP that he had lost 41 days of good-conduct credit, pushing his projected release date to March 2, 2028.
Combs is serving a four-year, two-month sentence after being convicted in 2025 on two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution-related encounters.
He was acquitted of more serious charges, including racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking.
His case featured testimony about violent conduct and sexual encounters prosecutors said were organised by the music mogul.
His legal team is appealing both the conviction and sentence, arguing that the punishment was too harsh.
The 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals heard arguments in April, but had yet to issue a ruling as of the latest reports.

468a0a83f2cd3cd6: BANGKOK, Oct 19 — Thailand’s government said today it could force the sale of up to 2,300 plots of land worth more than US$400 million (RM1.6 billion) as part of a crackdown on property held unlawfully by foreigners.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul called in a speech for tougher action against the use of Thai proxies to circumvent a ban on non-Thais owning land.
The government has identified 2,360 plots worth 14.01 billion baht owned through 1,397 proxies, Department of Lands Director Somchai Leelanoi said.
They cover an area totalling 5,467 rai — around 875 hectares — across the country.
“The department will expedite the forced sale of land in cases deemed illegal and will proceed with both civil and criminal legal action,” the government said in a statement.
Tourism accounted for 12.6 per cent of Thailand’s gross domestic product last year, and is forecast to hit almost 20 per cent by 2036, according to the World Travel and Tourism Council.

However, the industry has come under growing public scrutiny. There have been protests in recent months about bad behaviour by visitors, as well as concerns that foreigners are buying up property in certain hotspots, including Phuket.
Thai law bars foreign nationals or companies from owning land within the kingdom, except those with prior approval from the country’s Board of Investment.
However, a limited company can purchase land as long as the majority of shares are held by a Thai national.

“This investigation must not stop at merely the names of title deed holders or company shareholders; it must dig deeper to identify the true controlling figures, behind-the-scenes decision-makers, and ultimate beneficial owners,” Anutin said.
“Thailand remains open and welcoming to honest, transparent foreign investments that respect Thai law and abide by the rights granted under investment promotion regulations,” he said. — AFP

389df0739aba64b7: KUALA LUMPUR: Khee San Bhd has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Federation of Sundry Goods Merchants Associations of Malaysia and business owner Dr Paul Lim Pang Kiam to develop a digitalisation platform for independent sundry goods retailers.
The platform aims to help retailers adopt digital tools, prepare for e-Invoice requirements and improve operational efficiency and purchasing power.

Under the agreement, Khee San will sponsor and drive the programme, while the association will facilitate member participation, coordinate the selection of pilot retailers and suppliers, and represent members' interests in governance.

"The parties plan to establish a Malaysian private limited company to own and operate the platform, with Khee San as majority shareholder and responsible for day-to-day management," the company said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.

The platform is expected to integrate a retail management system and point-of-sale capabilities, e-Invoice and e-Vendor portals, as well as a group-buying Trading Hub that would pool orders from participating retailers to support bulk purchases and lower procurement costs.
However, the platform's detailed features and commercial arrangements remain subject to further development and definitive agreements.

The parties will also explore government subsidies, determine the pilot cohort and establish a special purpose vehicle, while negotiating definitive agreements covering commercial terms and data governance.
"The indicative roadmap envisages a pilot in months 1 to 6, broader Federation-wide rollout in months 7 to 12, and further scaling from year two, subject to planning and agreement," it said.

Khee San managing director Desmond Yong Loong Chen said the initiative would bring practical digital solutions to independent sundry goods retailers, including tools to improve daily operations and facilitate collective purchasing.
Lim, who originated the programme concept and brought the parties together, said a phased approach would allow the parties to test the model before any wider rollout.
267f6191c366bf66: PETALING JAYA: Seorang Ahli Parlimen kecewa apabila Belanjawan 2027 tidak turut mengandungi pengumuman bahawa kerajaan akan menggubal rang undang-undang (RUU) bagi menjamin peruntukan kawasan bagi semua wakil rakyat tanpa mengira kaitan politik.

Ketika membahaskan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat, Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi) berkata, beliau kekal bimbang kerana 'masih tiada undang-undang atau garis panduan yang mewajibkan peruntukan kawasan diberikan kepada semua wakil rakyat'.
Bagaimanapun, tegasnya, agihan peruntukan tidak sepatutnya sama rata bagi setiap kawasan Parlimen kerana ini tidak adil memandangkan terdapat perbezaan dari segi saiz kawasan dan jumlah pengundi.
“Hakikatnya, ada kawasan Parlimen yang jauh lebih besar daripada kawasan lain. Kalau salurkan jumlah yang sama kepada setiap kawasan, sudah pasti tidak adil,” katanya.
Pada Ogos, Naib Presiden Wawasan Wan Saiful Wan Jan mendakwa DAP sekadar 'bermain wayang' apabila parti itu terus menuntut peruntukan kawasan sama rata bagi semua Ahli Parlimen.
Wan Saiful berkata, tuntutan berkenaan pada dasarnya 'perkara yang baik', namun mempersoalkan mengapa DAP hanya membangkitkannya selepas lebih tiga tahun kerajaan perpaduan mentadbir.
"Tuntutan ini adalah perkara yang baik. Tapi ia wayang saja, sebab kalau DAP serius kenapa tak tuntut dari awal?" soalnya menerusi hantaran Facebook.

Wan Saiful berkata demikian selepas Pengerusi DAP Gobind Singh Deo menggesa Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menyalurkan peruntukan sama rata kepada semua Ahli Parlimen dan memaktubkan amalan tersebut menerusi perundangan.
Gobind berkata, kepimpinan DAP telah beberapa kali berbincang dengan Anwar mengenai janji Pakatan Harapan untuk memastikan agihan peruntukan yang adil kepada setiap wakil rakyat.

7325a76b2147bd6e: KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Material Holding Ltd, a unit of Mi Technovation Bhd, had launched its initial public offering (IPO) on the Singapore Exchange, pricing its shares at S$1.80 each, to raise a total of S$203.2 million (RM829.58 million).

The listing comprises a total offering of 77.5 million shares. This involves a fresh issuance of 51.5 million new shares by Mi Material, alongside 26 million existing shares offered by Mi Technovation as the vendor.

The issuance is structurally divided into two main tranches; an international offer comprising 71.27 million shares targeted at institutional and selected foreign investors outside the United States, as well as 6.22 million shares to the Singapore public.
Concurrently, a consortium of seven cornerstone investors has executed agreements to subscribe to an aggregate of 41.94 million new shares at the S$1.80 offering price.

The cornerstone backers include abrdn Asia Limited, abrdn Malaysia Sdn Bhd, Amova Asset Management Asia Limited, Areca Capital Sdn Bhd, Barings Singapore Pte Ltd, Fullerton Fund Management Company Ltd, and Manulife Investment Management (Singapore) Pte. Ltd.
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited and CGS International Securities Singapore Pte Ltd are acting as the Joint Global Coordinators, Bookrunners, and Underwriters for the exercise.
To support price stability upon the commencement of trading, Mi Technovation has granted the underwriters an over-allotment option.

CGS International Securities, acting as the stabilising manager, has the right to purchase up to 5 million additional shares—representing approximately 6.5 per cent of the total offering shares—at the S$1.80 price.
This stabilization window will remain active for 30 days from the listing date on SGX or until the maximum 5 million shares have been bought for stabilising actions.
The execution of this over-allotment option will not increase the total number of issued and outstanding shares immediately following the completion of the offering and cornerstone issuance.

Based on the S$1.80 offer price, the estimated net proceeds from the offering and the issuance of the cornerstone shares, after deducting underwriting fees and estimated offering expenses, will be approximately S$203.2 million.

Approximately S$157.9 million of the proceeds will be due to Mi Material. If the over-allotment option is exercised in full, the estimated net proceeds from the offering due to Mi Technovation will be approximately S$54 million (approximately RM220.45 million).
Mi Technovation will also undertake a dividend-in-specie, to be distributed to its entitled shareholders.
The proposed distribution will involve the distribution of up to 9 million shares to the shareholders of Mi Technovation whose names appear in the record of depositors as of 5.00 pm on Oct 12.
The distribution ratio is one distribution share for every 100 Mi Technovation shares held, excluding treasury shares.
Based on the respective shareholdings of the entitled shareholders as of Oct 12, 8.98 million shares will be distributed to the entitled shareholders.
Mi Material is one of the leading manufacturers of semiconductor advanced packaging materials, engaged in the design, development, manufacturing and commercialisation of precision solder spheres.
Solder spheres serve as critical interconnect components enabling electrical conductivity between integrated circuits and printed circuit boards.

"Our products and solutions are mainly used in end-use applications such as high-performance computing (HPC) for artificial intelligence (AI), memory (including high bandwidth memory (HBM)), mobile devices and wearables, and automotive applications," said the group.
Beyond its core solder spheres, Mi Material also produces solder-related materials and products, including solder ingots, copper core solder spheres, solder paste and solder preforms.

According to Yole, a market research, technology and strategy analysis, Mi Material's market share of the global solder sphere market based on the serviceable addressable market was 24 per cent in 2025.

Mi Materials have been part of Mi Technovation group since April 2021, operating as its semiconductor material business unit. The shareholders of Mi Technovation approved the spin-off of the business unit on Sept 17.

Mi Materials is headquartered in Singapore and currently has production facilities in Tainan, Taiwan and Ningbo, China. It has a combined annual production capacity of our production facilities ranging from approximately 6,600 billion to 8,900 billion solder spheres.

"To support our growth and diversify our production capability, we are in the process of establishing a third production facility in Senai, Johor, which is targeted to be ready for production by the fourth quarter of 2026, with production ramp-up in early 2027, and we plan to expand the production capacity of our facility in Taiwan," said Mi Material.
In addition, the group intends to build a research and development (R&D) and demonstration centre in Texas.

"Over the years, we have established ourselves as a key participant in the global semiconductor advanced packaging supply chain, with long-standing relationships, some of which span over 20 years, with integrated device manufacturers, semiconductor foundries and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers across markets including Taiwan, China, Malaysia, the European Union, Singapore, the United States, Japan, Korea and the Philippines," said Mi Material.
